subject.title: Telegram agent: chatbot follow-up loop + exec tool aborts on pkill against earlier-spawned process

question: Should this issue be split into a reply-policy item plus a process-control hardening item, and should OpenClaw enforce action-only/terse Telegram finals by rewriting model text, by prompt/tool guidance, or by leaving it to user memory/config?
rationale: The source-backed gaps are real, but choosing how aggressively to mutate natural-language final replies and whether raw shell `pkill -f` should be hardened versus steering to the managed process tool requires maintainer product and owner-boundary intent.

options.title: Split And Define Boundaries
options.body: Track the follow-up/closing behavior under the existing reply-finalization policy discussion and keep a separate narrow exec/process-control issue for raw shell self-match or managed-session termination proof.

options.title: One Coordinated Fix
options.body: Treat both symptoms as one agent-obedience bug and design a single runtime policy, accepting broader implementation and validation risk.

options.title: Keep As Maintainer Investigation
options.body: Leave this combined issue open as-is until live Telegram and Linux exec repro proof identifies whether the two symptoms share a real root cause.

recommendation.title: Split And Define Boundaries
recommendation.body: Track the follow-up/closing behavior under the existing reply-finalization policy discussion and keep a separate narrow exec/process-control issue for raw shell self-match or managed-session termination proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The reply-policy half likely extends adjacent reminder/follow-up guard work, which is the broader product decision in this combined issue.
